newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bank bill yields close lower as kiwi dlr rises.
newsitem.headline: NZ bank bill yields close lower as kiwi dlr rises.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.35 PCT (PREV 9.40) US 30-YR 6.42 (PREV 6.40)
* NZ short-dated yields fall as kiwi rises
* Wages data in line with forecasts
* Focus next week on coalitions talks, and possible easing
New Zealand short rates fell around six basis points on Friday as the kiwi dollar steamed to fresh 8-1/2 year highs.
However, volumes in the debt market were relatively light and dealers are wary of the volatile currency.
"The was no real reason to buy other than the kiwi remaining strong and sentiment that we are going to get an easing reasonably soon from the RB," an Auckland dealer said.
There were still further rumours of more euro and samurai issues, he said.
The bond market was extremely quiet and thin.

Wage rates data for the September year were exactly in line with market expectations, providing the Reserve Bank with yet another piece of evidence for why monetary conditions should be eased, dealers said.
Next week, the focus will be on whether the Reserve Bank should ease or not and the government coalition talks which will be entering their sixth week since the October 12 election.

The market is divided on whether the RB should ease before its December 17 Monetary Policy Statement and possibly before a government is formed or whether it should wait and hope the fiscal position is clearer by December 17.
"I would image they would like to see a government before they make any announcement so they have got some idea what sort of fiscal expansion we are going to see," said one dealer.
"If we do get an announcement on the government a reasonable distance prior to the (MPS) statement then I guess the likelihood of something coming out earlier is on the cards."
Another dealer said New Zealand bonds had underperformed Australia and he expects that when a government is formed the New Zealand market would continue to struggle vis-a-vis other countries' bonds.
